correctness.rationale: The frozen RESULT.md defines ordinary edge-matching faces of an explicit 11-vertex, 18-edge Herschel bipartite graph. Independent recreation of the 2^18 search, integral signed simplex boundaries, and deterministic toggle matching found 751 nonempty faces with f=(18,111,280,270,72), 367 matched Hasse covers, 2502 cover incidences, a complete acyclic orientation, and exactly (critical C0,C2,C3)=(1,2,14). The reconstructed integral Morse C3 -> C2 matrix (14 by 2) has two unit Smith factors, so the two 2-sphere generators can be cancelled against two 3-cells. No critical C1 cells occur; π2 of a wedge of two S2 is Z² and the attaching maps are determined by integral degrees. The remaining twelve 3-cells attach to a contractible skeleton, proving wedge^12 S3. Verification is exact and finite, not mod-2 alone. Graph rotation certificate and 3-connectivity establish the indicated nonouterplanar Herschel input.

originality.rationale: A canonical 3-connected Herschel ordinary matching complex, equivalently Ind(L(H)), is not a Herschel vertex independence complex and is not covered by an outerplanar matching-complex theorem. Resultary comparison found the Herschel ordinary independence complex and Goldner–Harary, Grötzsch, and other different graph matching complexes; their homotopy types cannot be transferred to Ind(L(H)). Bayer–Jelić Milutinović–Vega Theorem 2 treats outerplanar graphs, a hypothesis failing here. No independently inspected full primary result with the exact twelve-S3 homotopy classification was found; older Wachs survey and unindexed graph tables remain specific priority risks. Qualified best-of-knowledge original.

value.rationale: The Herschel graph is the canonical minimal non-Hamiltonian 3-connected polyhedral graph; an exact integral homotopy type of its ordinary matching complex tests the outerplanar-to-polyhedral boundary and distinguishes it from the mixed-dimensional Goldner–Harary matching example. Homotopy, not just rank or an arbitrary small numerical table, is established by an explicit integral acyclic Morse certificate.
